question: What caused the First World War? Explain.
answers: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo caused the war
It started because Gavrilo Princip shot the Archduke in 1914
The trigger was the shooting in Sarajevo so Austria declared war on Serbia
MAIN: militarism, alliances, imperialism and nationalism built up tension for years
Long term causes: arms race, competing alliances, empires clashing and nationalism
The alliance system dragged everyone in: Russia backed Serbia, Germany backed Austria
Germany wanted a bigger empire and navy so it is mostly Germany's fault
Germany gave Austria a blank cheque and invaded Belgium, so Germany caused it
The Schlieffen Plan shows Germany planned the war all along
Alliances meant a small Balkan crisis could not stay local, it escalated step by step
